claims.statement: For every rank-(m-1) physical matrix M and arbitrary Boolean core D, the squared spectrum is uniform on 2^(2m-2) atoms; H=2(m-1), U<=2(m-1), Ix and Iy are each at least (m-1)/2, and the retained-U endpoint loss for every finite adaptive/pruned shield-variable tree with one common disjoint factor h is at most 4Ix and at most 2I.

Combining the previously accepted full-column-rank theorem with the accepted nullity-one theorem yields a parameter-free retained-U constant 4 for every arbitrary-core bilinear shield satisfying rank(M)>=m-1.
Nullity at least two introduces a nonflat conditional fiber-spectrum entropy term for arbitrary cores; no dimension-independent single-use physical payment of that term is proved.
